prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick questions so my recommendations fit your situation:
- When did the crash happen?
- Were you injured (how severely) and did you get medical treatment?
- Was the other driver at fault and was there a police report?
- Do you want me to find and list local Pleasanton/Alameda County attorneys now?

While you decide, here’s practical guidance on how to pick the right personal-injury lawyer and what to do next.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care and follow up. Document injuries and treatment.  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, damage, road conditions, clothing, medical records, bills, and text/phone records.  
- Get the police report and witness contact info.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurance companies (yours or theirs) without advice from an attorney. Don’t sign releases or accept a quick low settlement offer.  
- Preserve your phone and any dash-cam / car-cam footage.

Which lawyer to hire — key qualities to look for
- Focus on personal injury and specifically car-accident cases (not just general practice).  
- Experience and trial capability — many insurers will offer more reasonable settlements if your lawyer will try the case.  
- Local knowledge of CA law and local courts (Alameda County/Southern Alameda courts).  
- Track record with cases like yours: similar injuries, liability issues, or complex medical cases.  
- Clear communication and accessibility — who in the office will handle your file?  
- Works on contingency (no upfront fee; lawyer paid from recovery) and transparent about fees and costs.  
- Good reviews, client references, and a clean State Bar record.

Questions to ask at the free consult
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine? What was the typical outcome?  
- Who will actually handle my case day-to-day? Can I meet them?  
- What’s your fee and how are costs handled? (Typical contingency: ~33% if settled before suit, up to 40% if suit is filed — but confirm specifics.)  
- What do you expect this case to be worth and what is your strategy?  
- How often will I get updates and how do you communicate?  
- Do you have client references or example verdicts/settlements?

What to bring to a consultation
- Police report (or report number)  
- Photos of the crash, damage, injuries, and scene  
- Medical records, imaging (X-rays, MRI), and bills  
- Insurance information (yours and other driver’s) and any correspondence from insurers  
- Names/contact info of witnesses  
- Your notes about how the crash happened and what you’ve missed at work (wage loss)

Timeline and deadlines
- California general rule: you usually have 2 years from the injury date to file a personal injury lawsuit (California Code of Civil Procedure § 335.1).  
- If a government entity is involved (city, county, transit agency), you may need to file an administrative claim within 6 months — that deadline is strict.  
- Acting quickly preserves evidence and gives your lawyer more time to investigate and negotiate.

How to check an attorney
- California State Bar website to confirm license and disciplinary record.  
- Read client reviews and look at verdicts/settlements the firm publishes.  
- Ask for references.

Do you want local attorney options?
If you’d like, I can pull together a short list (3–6) of personal-injury attorneys or firms near Pleasanton (with contact info and any notable practice points). Tell me whether you prefer larger firms or a smaller boutique, and I’ll prepare that list.
